title: Mouse Without Borders disconnects when I type "%"
author: zudora

judgment.rationale: The reporter observed repeated disconnects associated with typing % in PowerPoint on 0.88, but the exact key sequence and keyboard layout are missing. The current MWB path forwards generic keyboard events and has no percent-specific branch in the inspected code; the available evidence does not establish whether the trigger is a layout-dependent chord, PowerPoint-specific, or an MWB input/connection issue.
evidence: The issue body reports disconnects in five of eight attempts while typing % in PowerPoint, with $ as a comparison input, on PowerToys 0.88.
The issue is open, unassigned, has no comments, and is labeled Needs-Repro.
The inspected Event.KeybdEvent path sends generic keyboard data and Receiver forwards it to InputSimulation.SendKey; no percent-specific handling was found.
judgment.recommended_action: Ask for the exact keyboard sequence/layout, a comparison outside PowerPoint, the Windows build, and a fresh /bugreport captured immediately after a recurrence before selecting an input-path fix.

fix_assessment.rationale: The specific keyboard sequence and relationship to the connection drop are not established; no code change is justified yet.

issue_context.summary: The reporter says Mouse Without Borders disconnected five of eight times while typing % in PowerPoint on PowerToys 0.88; the exact input sequence and keyboard layout are not recorded.
known_information: The report associates the disconnect with typing % in PowerPoint and says $ did not produce the same result.
The reported environment used PowerToys 0.88; Windows version/build and keyboard layout were not included.
The issue is open, unassigned, has no comments, and is categorized under Mouse Without Borders and Needs-Repro.
inferences: Because the key sequence and layout are unknown, the trigger could be an application-specific interaction, a modifier/key transition, or an unrelated intermittent connection failure.
issue_context.analysis: The current sender/receiver path handles generic key data rather than a percent character. The next decision depends on identifying the physical/logical sequence and whether the disconnect is application-specific; a speculative code change is not justified yet.
initial_investigation: Inspected Mouse Without Borders Event.KeybdEvent and Receiver keyboard delivery paths; they forward generic keyboard data to InputSimulation.SendKey.
No percent-specific branch or linked fix was found; issue #51077 groups this report with connection drops/no reconnect, but does not establish a root cause.

information_gaps.information: The active keyboard layout and exact keys pressed to produce %.
information_gaps.why_needed: The same character can be produced by different key/modifier sequences, and MWB forwards key events rather than text characters.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Report the Windows keyboard layout and the exact physical/logical keys used to enter %; do not assume a particular layout.

information_gaps.information: Whether the same % sequence disconnects MWB outside PowerPoint.
information_gaps.why_needed: This distinguishes a PowerPoint-specific interaction from a system-wide or MWB keyboard-input path issue.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: With MWB connected, enter % in Notepad using the same keyboard sequence and report whether it disconnects there as well.

information_gaps.information: A fresh PowerToys diagnostic package captured immediately after a recurrence, plus the Windows version/build.
information_gaps.why_needed: The diagnostic context may identify why the MWB connection dropped and the Windows build is needed to interpret input behavior.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Capture the diagnostic report after a recurrence and attach it using the instructions from /bugreport.

information_gaps.information: The Windows edition, version, and OS build.
information_gaps.why_needed: Input behavior can vary by Windows build and helps distinguish the environment from a MWB-specific failure.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Include the Windows edition, version, and OS build from Settings > System > About.

actions.label: Request keyboard layout and disconnect trace
